idiom_name: JPA/Hibernate entity mapping configured for Kotlin (kotlin("plugin.jpa") no-arg + all-open)
implementation_notes: In Kotlin the mapper is the JPA provider: Hibernate owns the object-relational translation and the EntityManager supplies identity map, change tracking and flush, while the mapping is declared with annotations or an external orm.xml. Kotlin needs two compiler adjustments - the no-arg plugin (the kotlin("plugin.jpa") preset) so Hibernate can instantiate entities, and all-open so lazy-loading proxies can subclass them - which is why plain data classes make poor entities: keep entities as open classes with mutable properties and put behaviour, not persistence calls, inside them. JetBrains Exposed's DAO module is the Kotlin-native alternative, but its Entity is bound to its Table, so it is closer to Active Record and only fits when persistence ignorance is not a requirement.
pitfalls: data class is a trap for entities: generated equals/hashCode/copy over all properties conflicts with JPA identity and proxies - implement equality on a business key.
Without the all-open and no-arg plugins Hibernate fails at runtime (InstantiationException) or cannot build proxies, and the error points at the framework rather than the Kotlin class.
Lazy associations initialised outside the transaction raise LazyInitializationException; keep the load inside the mapper's transaction or declare a fetch plan.
Kotlin null-safety cuts both ways: a non-null property mapped to a nullable column fails on dirty data, while a lateinit/!! property hides the mapping's nullability contract from the compiler.
